2609.04047.title: The Dice Roll Method: A Standardized Protocol for Repeated-Query Auditing of Large Language Model Brand Recommendations
2609.04047.paper_summary: Background: Researchers increasingly use repeated identical prompts to audit stochastic variation in large language model (LLM) brand recommendations, yet no standardized protocol exists for setting iteration counts, selecting stability metrics, or establishing reliability thresholds. Objective: We formalize the Dice Roll Method as a reusable protocol for repeated-query auditing of LLM brand recommendations, grounded in a generative model of temperature-scaled nucleus sampling. Methods: Total response variance is decomposed into sampling, prompt-phrasing, run-to-run, and model-version components. The stack: a negative-binomial mixed model with iterations as repeated measures; Cliff's delta as the distribution-free effect size; dependence-preserving bootstrap; simulation-based power; a generalizability-theory decomposition; drift diagnostics on pinned snapshots. We reanalyse five brand-recommendation auditing studies: approximately 190,000 observations, 270+ brands, 6 languages, iteration counts 5 to 40. Results: Three tiers of iteration guidance emerge from the D-study: exploratory (n = 5, G = 0.58), confirmatory (n = 10, G = 0.74), and rigorous (n = 15, G = 0.81), tied to effect-size and generalizability targets. The four metric families (count, set, embedding, fairness-adjusted PASOR) are complementary, motivating a compact metric battery over single indicators. A pre-registered external validation on three independent corpora (Motoki et al., 100-round; Rozado, 24 models; llm-stability) reproduces the D-study reliability prediction in 37 of 39 cells with no failures and the n = 5 power value to two decimals; the fixed tiers do not transfer, supporting a pilot-then-solve reading. Conclusion: The protocol gives repeated-query auditing of LLM brand recommendations a statistically principled footing under the conditional, non-Gaussian structure of real autoregressive generation.
2609.04047.paper_summary_zh: 背景：研究人員越來越多地使用重複相同的提示來審核大型語言模型（LLM）品牌推薦中的隨機變異，但目前尚無標準化的協議來設定迭代次數、選擇穩定性指標或建立可靠性閾值。<lb/>目標：我們將擲骰子方法正式化為一種可重用的協議，用於重複查詢審核LLM品牌推薦，基於溫度縮放的核取樣生成模型。<lb/>方法：總響應變異被分解為取樣、提示措辭、運行到運行和模型版本組件。<lb/>堆疊：一個負二項混合模型，將迭代作為重複測量；Cliff's delta作為無分佈效應大小；保持依賴的自助法；基於模擬的效能；一般化理論分解；在固定快照上的漂移診斷。<lb/>我們重新分析了五個品牌推薦審核研究：約190,000個觀察，270多個品牌，6種語言，迭代次數5到40。<lb/>結果：從D研究中出現了三個層級的迭代指導：探索性（n = 5，G = 0.58）、確認性（n = 10，G = 0.74）和嚴謹性（n = 15，G = 0.81），與效應大小和一般化目標相關。<lb/>四個指標家族（計數、集合、嵌入、公平調整的PASOR）是互補的，促進了一個緊湊的指標電池而非單一指標。<lb/>在三個獨立語料庫上的預註冊外部驗證（Motoki等，100輪；Rozado，24個模型；llm-stability）在39個單元中重現了D研究的可靠性預測，沒有失敗，n = 5的效能值精確到小數點後兩位；固定層級不轉移，支持先試點再解決的閱讀。<lb/>結論：該協議使LLM品牌推薦的重複查詢審核在真實自回歸生成的條件非高斯結構下具有統計原則基礎。
